beats.got: This is JTBD. I know it, I've read the Christensen stuff.

beats.trigger: *"Share the whole agent"* is a vendor pitch and is not on the list.
beats.got: Push and pull let someone get value from an agent without running one. That's the non-engineer route I came here for.

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?
beats.got: A way to test whether someone would swap their current tool for mine. I normally build first and ask after.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.

beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new, it's the lecture title

beats.trigger: The fourth does not copy at all
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy in an afternoon, but someone answering for the agent doesn't. That's the piece I have never assigned.

beats.trigger: Output and interface ask them to run nothing.
beats.got: Each strategy asks something different of the receiver. I'd already got most of this from the exercise.

beats.trigger: Many companies have rolled out access far ahead of trust.
beats.got: Access is one switch and takes a minute, while use takes weeks. Our license counts look good and tell us nothing about use.

beats.trigger: That second list is the work a sharing plan has to carry, and most of it belongs in the people plan.
beats.got: nothing new, it's a reflection prompt

beats.trigger: The leadership had not done the analysis. People they trusted had.
beats.got: A fifteen-person multi-agent redesign got no decision because leadership hadn't done the analysis themselves. That's a failure mode I hadn't met, and it's the org-wide one I care about.

beats.trigger: Your candidate is not competing with nothing. It is competing with that.
beats.got: Whatever the person does today is the competitor, not other AI tools. The 'answers come back small and specific' part is useful.

beats.trigger: Ask the question before you show them anything you built.
beats.got: Ask one person how they do the job before showing them anything. That's the opposite of what I do.

beats.trigger: Compare your choice with a neighbour's, then run the debrief.
beats.got: nothing new, it's a group comparison step and I'd rather build

beats.trigger: Test the switch, not the solution.
beats.got: nothing new, it's a recap

beats.trigger: One real conversation tells you more about absorption than a finished plan does.
beats.got: A real conversation beats a polished plan, and I should bring what the person said.

beats.trigger: In Module 8 you ask what changes when you don't have to build each agent by hand.
beats.got: A teaser for Module 8 that I'm actually curious about.

take_homes: Before I build for non-engineers, I ask one of them how they do the job today. I don't build first and ask after.
Push and pull are how people who don't run agents get value from them. I should pick between them based on what the person is trying to get done.
The technical plan is the easy half. If a plan has no named owner for the agent and for the people side, it isn't a plan.

monday.move: Message one sales lead asking for twenty minutes on how they prepare for a customer call today, and show them nothing. I'll also find out who would own the setup before I build anything.
monday.who: A sales team lead (name to be picked) and one person to own maintenance, still unassigned
monday.when: Monday morning, message sent before standup
monday.stop_condition: If they say they don't need it, or I can't find a maintainer, I don't build the weekend version.
monday.blocker: I'll want to skip the conversation and just build the sales thing. Nobody has asked for it, and nobody has said they'll maintain it.

misconception.why: The story is a good agent system with a plausible output, and the decision still never came because the humans hadn't made it theirs. Checking output quality didn't matter there, so my 'good agent means good output' idea is incomplete. I still think the checking steps in the exercises are ceremony for someone who runs agents daily, so I'd call it shaken, not changed.

one_line: Not much new on the agent side, but it was uncomfortably useful on why my weekend builds for non-engineers would have sat unused. I'd send it to a CTO whose engineers already run agents.
